Title: Hepatic Notch2 deficiency leads to bile duct agenesis perinatally and secondary bile duct formation after weaning.

Journal/Date: Developmental biology (2014)

--- ABSTRACT ---
[UNLABELLED]: Notch signaling plays an acknowledged role in bile-duct development, but its involvement in cholangiocyte-fate determination remains incompletely understood. We investigated the effects of early Notch2 deletion in Notch2(fl/fl)/Alfp-Cre(tg/-) ("Notch2-cKO") and Notch2(fl/fl)/Alfp-Cre(-/-) ("control") mice. Fetal and neonatal Notch2-cKO livers were devoid of cytokeratin19 (CK19)-, Dolichos-biflorus agglutinin (DBA)-, and SOX9-positive ductal structures, demonstrating absence of prenatal cholangiocyte differentiation. Despite extensive cholestatic hepatocyte necrosis and growth retardation, mortality was only ~15%. Unexpectedly, a slow process of secondary cholangiocyte differentiation and bile-duct formation was initiated around weaning that histologically resembled the ductular reaction. Newly formed ducts varied from rare and non-connected, to multiple, disorganized tubular structures that connected to the extrahepatic bile ducts. Jaundice had disappeared in ~30% of Notch2-cKO mice by 6 months. The absence of NOTCH2 protein in postnatally differentiating cholangiocyte nuclei of Notch2-cKO mice showed that these cells had not originated from non-recombined precursor cells. Notch2 and Hnf6 mRNA levels were permanently decreased in Notch2-cKO livers. Perinatally, Foxa1, Foxa2, Hhex, Hnf1β, Cebpα and Sox9 mRNA levels were all significantly lower in Notch2-cKO than control mice, but all except Foxa2 returned to normal or increased levels after weaning, coincident with the observed secondary bile-duct formation. Interestingly, Hhex and Sox9 mRNA levels remained elevated in icteric 6 months old Notch2-cKOs, but decreased to control levels in non-icteric Notch2-cKOs, implying a key role in secondary bile-duct formation.
[CONCLUSION]: Cholangiocyte differentiation becomes progressively less dependent on NOTCH2 signaling with age, suggesting that ductal-plate formation is dependent on NOTCH2, but subsequent cholangiocyte differentiation is not.

key_findings.finding: PMID 23500150 is a distinct primary study of liver-specific Notch2 deficiency during chemically induced biliary injury, not the developmental agenesis model. It reports a liver-specific Notch-2-cKO (with DDC or ANIT injury) in which progenitor cells accumulated but failed to mature into biliary ducts; K19 and SOX9 were used for quantification. It supports an ongoing requirement for Notch2 in biliary tubule morphogenesis/repair, but does not establish perinatal duct agenesis or post-weaning developmental rescue.

source_tools.relevance: Primary-study abstract and results preview distinguish injury-repair model from developmental model
Annotations identify Notch2, Krt19, Sox9, and injury chemicals in this paper

key_findings.finding: Jag1/Notch signaling papers should not be substituted for the direct Notch2 knockout evidence. PMID 31469182 studies Jag1+/- Alagille-model livers with Sox9 dosage manipulation, and PMID 34549776 concerns Jag1/Notch2 hypomorphic combinations; these address biliary paucity/modification of Alagille phenotypes rather than isolated hepatocyte/liver-specific Notch2 deletion. The direct answer to the agenesis-then-secondary-formation question comes from PMID 25446530.

source_tools.relevance: Annotations identify Jag1, Notch2, and Sox9 context for the Alagille modifier study
Search result describes the Jag1 plus hypomorphic Notch2 model as a distinct double-heterozygous context

entities.name: Notch2
observations: In hepatic Notch2 conditional knockout mice, fetal and neonatal livers lacked CK19-, DBA-, and SOX9-positive ductal structures; secondary cholangiocyte differentiation and duct formation began around weaning despite persistent Notch2 deficiency.

entities.name: Notch2 duct agenesis
observations: Notch2fl/fl;Alfp-Cretg/- mice showed absent fetal/neonatal intrahepatic duct markers, supporting perinatal bile-duct agenesis; secondary, disorganized ducts formed beginning around weaning, with some connecting to extrahepatic ducts.
Approximately 30% of cKO mice were no longer jaundiced by 6 months; postnatal cholangiocytes lacked nuclear NOTCH2, arguing against rescue by unrecombined Notch2-positive cells.

source_tools.relevance: Direct answer to the developmental question
